meta.name: HQ visuals manifest
meta.purpose: Maps HQ diorama plates (docs/hq-diorama-vision.md) to the art asset that renders them and to their hand-authored hit regions, so no HQ screen ever hardcodes a path or a region rect. Follows data/combat_visuals.json's precedent exactly (see that file's own meta block).
meta.plateRule: One entry per key under 'rooms' (v1 ships only 'bedsit' -- docs/hq-diorama-vision.md §10). 'image' is a res:// path to the room's 390x660 display-resolution plate (authored 195x330, shown 2x nearest per §3), or "" when no plate has been produced yet -- the room then fills with the flat data/palette.json colour named by 'fallbackColor' instead, same two-level fallback combat_visuals.json's backdrops use. 'width'/'height' are the plate's display-resolution size in logical px.
meta.regionRule: 'regions' keys are the room's zones (§3.1 -- dial/lab/security/rest/rooms/oreStore/gym for the bedsit tier; not enumerated here so a later tier or sub-view plate can add its own without touching any reader code). Each region is {x, y, width, height, label, image} in the plate's own display-resolution coordinate space -- the same rect is both the tap hit region and the sprite rect, since a region's art (once produced) is baked directly into the plate or into its own small overlay sprite at that exact rect (§3.2/§11: baked outlines, hit regions measured against the finished plate). 'image' empty means no dedicated sprite for this region yet -- HqDiorama draws a labelled placeholder box there instead, per docs/hq-diorama-vision.md §9 ('the entire HQ tab is therefore navigable, tappable and playable with zero art produced'). 'label' is the human-readable text the placeholder box and debug overlay both show. An optional 'installedImage' (security only, so far) is a second full-region plate HqDiorama itself never reads -- hq.gd's own _security_lock_installed_plate() deep-copies the plate and swaps 'image' for 'installedImage' when state.home.security has 'lock' installed, since HqDiorama is a pure renderer that never touches GameState (same deep-copy-and-swap trick hq.gd's _hostile_door_plate() already used for the raid-pending label).
meta.gymDeviation: hq-diorama ticket 02: §3.1's own table lists Gym's 'First tier present' as 'flat', one tier above bedsit -- v1 (§10) ships the bedsit plate only, so a strict reading has no gym region here. Ticket 02's own prose lists Gym among the zones to wire up regardless, and the human maintainer explicitly chose (2026-09-07) to wire it into the bedsit plate now rather than leave Train unreachable until a Flat-tier plate art ticket ships -- a deliberate, approved deviation from the tier table, not an oversight.
meta.regionSizeRule: Every region must be >= 44x44 logical px and must not overlap another region in the same room (§3.2) -- enforced by GameData._validate_hq_visuals().
meta.artReview: ART-REVIEW (ticket 10): bedsit plate produced (assets/hq/bedsit_room.png) and all region rects re-measured against it by pixel inspection of the finished art -- NOT yet confirmed against the live in-app debug overlay (CLAUDE.md workflow rule 5: agent cannot see the running UI), so the human should still toggle hq.gd's debug overlay on-device once and eyeball each of the 6 rects below against the real render. oreStore has no fixture drawn in the source art at all (no bag/strongbox/safe was produced) -- 'image' stays empty and it renders as a placeholder box until that art exists; region rect is a guessed empty floor spot, not measured against anything. Security ships both states: 'image' (no lock, matches state.home.security=[] at new-game start, REFERENCE.md §2) and 'installedImage' (Reinforced Lock fitted), swapped at render time by hq.gd's _security_lock_installed_plate() -- see regionRule above.
meta.labBench: hq-diorama ticket 06, docs/hq-diorama-vision.md §5.1: the Lab bench sub-view plate, a sibling of 'rooms' rather than a member of it -- it's reached from the 'lab' room zone, not a property tier. One wide plate (1170x844 display-resolution, 3x the 390-wide screen) with three 390px-wide focal stops (books/ore/apparatus, left to right) the screen pans between by offsetting the rendered HqDiorama's x position by whole stop-widths -- never free-scrolled (§5.1: 'no free scrolling -- a swipe gesture would fight the ore-dragging'). The books stop (x 0-390) carries the two notebooks, §5.2's mode fork. ART-REVIEW applies to every rect in this file -- none of it has been checked against a live overlay.
meta.labBenchOre: ticket 07, §5.4: the ore stop (x 390-780) -- five containers, region ids 'ore_<oreTypeId>' so scenes/screens/hq_lab_bench.gd can derive the ore type straight from the region id with no lookup table. 'image' stays empty (no fixture drawn) alongside three new optional per-count-state fields -- 'emptyImage'/'someImage'/'plentyImage' -- following the same deep-copy-and-swap convention data/hq_visuals.json's 'installedImage' already established for the door's security region: the screen picks whichever of the three matches the player's current ore count and swaps it into 'image' for that render pass only, never mutating GameData.HQ_VISUALS itself. All three stay empty until a state-variant sprite is produced, so every container renders as a placeholder box today, its label text carrying the empty/some/plenty state instead (§9's degradation rule).
meta.labBenchApparatus: ticket 07, §5.3: the apparatus stop (x 780-1170) -- one region per data/approaches.json approach, region ids 'apparatus_<approachId>' (same derive-from-id convention as the ore containers above). All four are authored here regardless of room gating; hq_lab_bench.gd deletes an apparatus's region from its own render-time copy of this plate when Approaches.is_known() is false for that approach, per §3.2's 'a hit region for an object not present at this tier does not exist' -- so this manifest is the full four-apparatus roster the property ladder eventually reveals, not what's tappable on a fresh bedsit save (which only ever shows heat/grinding, the two start-known approaches).
